segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a single large pink 'person' mask on the left half of all five frames, combining the leaning technician (~3–5 metres away, partly cut off by the left frame edge) with the camera wearer's own left forearm and hand resting on the central armrest (~3–5 metres away) whenever they are in contact. Because both arms are far, out of reach, and touching in frames 1–4, the mask merges the technician's reaching left arm and torso with the wearer's left hand into one connected region, while the gap between the technician's right and left arms forms a black cutout underneath her torso. Across the sequence, as the technician releases the wearer's hand and sits upright in frame 5, the pink mask shifts upward and left, though the wearer's left arm remains erroneously attached to the bottom of her mask and mislabelled as a purple 'banana'. While the map highlights the combined occupancy of the interacting arms on the left, it is highly unreliable elsewhere: it completely misses the camera wearer's legs and right hand on the right, hallucinating a 'cup' on a floor stool in frame 1 and labelling the yellow nail file (frame 4) and the wearer's left forearm (frame 5) as 'banana'.
pose: The pose map tracks the upper-body skeleton (yellow) and left-hand joints (magenta) of the technician on the left side of the scene, located roughly 3 to 5 metres from the camera wearer. In frames 1–4, her torso and shoulder links angle downward and to the left, showing her leaning deeply forward with her head near the left edge facing down toward the armrest and toward the camera wearer's face. Her left arm extends right into the centre of the frame—far beyond the reach of both people—where the detailed magenta hand skeleton overlaps the wearer's left hand in frames 1–4, while her right arm extends downward toward the wearer's left foot in frames 1–3 before dropping out of tracking in frame 4. In frame 5, as the technician lifts her torso and brings both hands together above the armrest, the entire yellow body skeleton fails to detect, leaving only a cluster of magenta hand keypoints where her two hands meet. This map makes the technician's hunched torso geometry, shoulder orientation, and fine finger articulation much clearer than in the dark-clothed RGB view, but it is unreliable in missing the camera wearer's own body and hands entirely and losing the technician's body pose in frame 5.
